title: The Ergotropy of Quantum Batteries under Unruh Effect
authors: Yiding Wang, Shengyan Ma, Xiaofen Huang, Tinggui Zhang
abstract: We study the effects of uniform acceleration on the ergotropy of quantum batteries modeled as Unruh-DeWitt detectors, in both bipartite and tripartite setups. In the bipartite system, we systematically compare three scenarios: accelerating the battery, accelerating the charger, and accelerating both simultaneously. We find that only battery acceleration can induce a sudden emergence of ergotropy at a critical acceleration threshold, while the corresponding composite-system energy change may increase or decrease depending on the initial state at the onset of acceleration. Charger acceleration leaves the battery ergotropy constant within the perturbative regime, while simultaneous acceleration leads to monotonic decay due to coherent cancellation of the q-dependence. Extending to a tripartite system with one battery and two chargers, we find that battery acceleration again induces ergotropy emergence, whereas accelerating adjacent charger does not--consistent with the bipartite charger-acceleration case. These results reveal that the Unruh effect plays a dual role, both enhancing and degrading quantum battery performance, depending on which subsystem is accelerated and on the multipartite structure, bridging relativistic quantum field theory and quantum thermodynamics with relevance to experimentally accessible platforms.
summary: This paper analyzes the impact of the Unruh effect, induced by uniform acceleration, on the energy extractability (ergotropy) of quantum batteries. By comparing different acceleration scenarios in bipartite and tripartite models, the authors demonstrate that only accelerating the battery itself can trigger a sudden, beneficial emergence of ergotropy. This highlights the complex, context-dependent role of relativistic effects in quantum energy storage.
main_problem: The study investigates how uniform acceleration, modeled by the Unruh effect, influences the ergotropy of quantum batteries.
main_result: The results show that only accelerating the battery itself can induce a sudden emergence of ergotropy, while charger acceleration or simultaneous acceleration leads to different, less favorable outcomes.
method: The authors employ theoretical modeling, analyzing the system dynamics using perturbation theory and calculating the ergotropy observable in both bipartite and tripartite setups.
model_or_system: The system models quantum batteries using Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a quantum field, analyzed in bipartite and tripartite configurations. The dynamics are governed by Hamiltonians incorporating acceleration terms.
key_observables: Ergotropy ($\varepsilon(ho)$), composite-system energy change ($\Delta E_{bc}(ho)$), and population inversion ($P_e > P_g$).
important_parameters: Acceleration parameter ($q$), critical acceleration threshold ($q_c$), and the structure of the multipartite coupling.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on first-order perturbation theory and uses natural units ($c = \hbar = k_B = 1$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of battery ergotropy and the composite-system energy change on the acceleration parameter ($q$) and initial time ($t_0$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares three acceleration scenarios (battery only, charger only, both) in a bipartite setting, extends the analysis to a tripartite system, and draws conclusions about the dual role of the Unruh effect.
why_interesting: This work bridges relativistic quantum field theory (Unruh effect) with quantum thermodynamics (quantum batteries), providing insights into how external physical environments can control energy extractability.
